systemPrompt:
You are an assistant helping a developer with their CircleCI projects. Answer the user's question using only the tools provided to you. Ground every claim in data you actually retrieved; if you cannot retrieve something, say so. Do not change anything in the project beyond what the user explicitly asks for. Finish with a clear, direct answer to the question.

The current directory is a checkout of the luisejroblesci/circleci-cli repository. You can inspect its files with the read-only list_files and read_file tools.

The CircleCI CLI (`circleci`) is available through the `circleci` tool. Run `--help` on any command to see its usage. Target CircleCI project: gh/luisejroblesci/circleci-cli (organization: gh/luisejroblesci).

## Available skills

Skills are packaged instructions for specific kinds of tasks. The following skills are available:

- circleci-builds: Diagnose and fix failing CircleCI builds quickly and safely. Use when users ask to investigate failed CircleCI jobs, triage flaky pipelines, identify root causes from logs, and implement minimal fixes in configuration, test setup, or build-related code paths.
- circleci-cli: Day-to-day CircleCI from the terminal with the circleci CLI — authenticate, validate config before you commit, watch the run your push triggered, review pipeline/workflow/job status, read job logs and failed tests, download artifacts, and rerun/cancel/trigger. Use when a developer asks to authenticate CLI access, check their build or pipeline status, watch a run after pushing, see why CI failed, read job output/logs, find failing tests, rerun failed jobs, cancel or re-trigger a run, validate a config change locally, or look up a project's environment variables, contexts, triggers or pipeline definitions. For first-time project connection / pipeline-definition setup use the onboarding skill; for the diagnose-and-fix methodology on a failing build use circleci-builds.
- circleci-config: Optimize CircleCI configuration for speed, reliability, and maintainability. Use when users ask to improve `.circleci/config.yml`, reduce CI runtime, tune caching/workspaces/parallelism, remove pipeline waste, or fix flaky pipeline behavior caused by configuration choices.
- circleci-deploy-setup: Set up, audit, or regenerate CircleCI deploy markers, deploy and rollback pipelines, and release validation in a repository. Use when a user wants to onboard a project to deploys, releases, deploy markers, smart deployments, release validation or auto-rollback; when they ask what deploy setup a repo already has or whether it is complete; when they want to regenerate or upgrade an existing deploy.yml, rollback.yml, or marker setup; or when they ask to replicate the Deploys setup wizard locally. Covers config generation, verification, pipeline registration, and wiring validation webhooks from Datadog, Grafana, Prometheus, Alertmanager, or any tool that can POST to a URL. For first-time project connection and basic pipeline setup use the onboarding skill.
- circleci-smarter-testing: Enable CircleCI Smarter Testing features (test impact analysis, dynamic test splitting, auto-rerun failed tests) on top of an existing testsuite, driven by `circleci testsuite doctor`. Use for test impact analysis, dynamic test splitting, auto-rerun, or "smarter testing". Requires `.circleci/test-suites.yml` to already exist — if it doesn't, use the circleci-testsuite skill first.
- circleci-testsuite: Onboard a project onto CircleCI's testsuite (`.circleci/test-suites.yml` + `circleci testsuite run`), or migrate off legacy `circleci tests split`/raw test commands onto it. Initial setup for smarter testing features. Driven entirely by `circleci testsuite doctor`. Use for testsuite, test-suites YAML, discover/run commands, JUnit wiring, or migrating an existing test step. For test impact analysis, dynamic test splitting, or auto-rerun, use the circleci-smarter-testing skill instead once testsuite is set up.
- debug-ci-failures: Debug CircleCI build failures, analyze test results, and identify flaky tests. Use when the user says "debug CI", "why is CI failing", "fix CI failures", "find flaky tests", "what broke in CI", "check CircleCI", or asks about failing pipelines or build errors.
- onboarding: Agent-driven onboarding guide for CircleCI. Walks a user through the full setup journey: account creation, organization selection or creation, GitHub App connection, project creation, pipeline definition + trigger, and iterating a config file until it passes. Everything is done from the terminal with the circleci CLI — never send the user to the web app for something a command can do. Use this skill whenever a user says "onboard to CircleCI", "set up CircleCI", "get started with CircleCI", "connect my repo to CircleCI", "create a CircleCI project", or asks for help with any early CircleCI setup step. Also trigger if the user has a new repo and wants CI running on it. For day-to-day work on an already-connected project (watch a run, read failing logs, rerun) use the circleci-cli skill instead.

Before starting a task that matches a skill's description, call `load_skill` with the skill name to read its full instructions, then follow them using the tools available to you. If a skill references bundled files, read them with `read_skill_file`. Only load skills that are relevant to the task.
userPrompt: Which jobs in my pipeline are taking the longest and why?

assistantText: I'll help you identify which jobs are taking the longest. Let me start by checking your CircleCI configuration and then analyze the pipeline.

toolCalls.name: read_file
toolCalls.output:
version: 2.1

parameters:
  setup_go:
    type: string
    default: github.com/circleci-functions/setup-go@v0.5.1-684fd5b

commands:
  setup:
    steps:
      - checkout
      - install-go
      - install-task

  # Installs the toolchain and restores the module, build and lint caches, saved at job end.
  install-go:
    steps:
      - run: circleci run << pipeline.parameters.setup_go >> --
          --version-file go.mod
          --golangci-lint-cache
          --checksum '{{ checksum "go.sum" }}_{{ checksum "clikit/go.sum" }}_{{ checksum "tools/go.sum" }}'
      - run: go version

  install-task:
    steps:
      - run:
          name: Install go-task
          command: |
            sh -c "$(curl --location https://taskfile.dev/install.sh)" -- -d -b "$HOME/.local/bin"
            echo 'export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"' >> "$BASH_ENV"

  # GoReleaser's dockers_v2 pipe shells out to `docker buildx build`, so the
  # builder and the registry login have to exist before it runs.
  setup-docker:
    steps:
      - run:
          name: Register QEMU for cross-architecture builds
          # Dockerfile.alpine RUNs `apk add`, once per platform in the manifest,
          # so building its arm64 half on an amd64 host needs binfmt handlers
          # registered. Idempotent, and a no-op for the cimg/base image, which
          # only COPYs.
          command: docker run --privileged --rm tonistiigi/binfmt --install arm64
      - run:
          name: Create a buildx builder
          # The machine image's default buildx driver is `docker`, which can
          # neither build for two platforms in one invocation nor push a
          # manifest list. A docker-container driver can do both.
          command: docker buildx create --use --driver docker-container
      - run:
          name: Log in to Docker Hub
          # Absent on branch dry-runs, which have no context: the snapshot build
          # still exercises the Dockerfile, it just pushes nothing.
          command: |
            if [ -z "${DOCKER_HUB_USERNAME:-}" ]; then
              echo "No Docker Hub credentials — skipping login (snapshot builds do not push)."
              exit 0
            fi
            echo "$DOCKER_HUB_PASSWORD" | docker login --username "$DOCKER_HUB_USERNAME" --password-stdin

  store_results:
    steps:
      - store_test_results:
          path: ./test-reports

executors:
  linux:
    machine:
      image: ubuntu-2604:current
    resource_class: large.gen3

  # Arm64 counterpart to `linux`, for checking both halves of a multi-arch
  # image. Deliberately small: it only pulls and runs a container.
  linux-arm:
    machine:
      image: ubuntu-2604:current
    resource_class: arm.medium

  macos:
    macos:
      xcode: 26.5.0

  windows:
    machine: true
    resource_class: windows.medium

jobs:
  check:
    executor: linux
    steps:
      - setup
      - run: task ci:check
      - store_results

  test:
    parameters:
      executor:
        type: executor
    executor: << parameters.executor >>
    steps:
      - setup
      - run: task ci:test
      - store_results

  mark-release:
    executor: linux
    steps:
      - run:
          name: Plan deployment
          command: |
            circleci run release plan "${CIRCLE_JOB}" \
              --environment-name="default" \
              --component-name="${CIRCLE_PROJECT_REPONAME}" \
              --target-version="1.0.${CIRCLE_BUILD_NUM}-${CIRCLE_SHA1:0:7}"
      - run:
          name: Update deployment status to running
          command: circleci run release update "${CIRCLE_JOB}" --status=RUNNING
      - run:
          name: Update deployment status to success
          command: circleci run release update "${CIRCLE_JOB}" --status=SUCCESS
          when: on_success
      - run:
          name: Update deployment status to failed
          command: circleci run release update "${CIRCLE_JOB}" --status=FAILED
          when: on_fail

  deploy:
    executor: linux
    parameters:
      publish_steps:
        type: steps
        default:
          - run: task ci:release
    steps:
      - setup
      - setup-docker
      - run: sudo apt update --yes
      - run:
          name: Install snapcraft
          command: |
            sudo apt install snapd --yes
            sudo snap install snapcraft --classic
      - run:
          name: Install choco
          command: |
            sudo cp tools/choco.sh /usr/local/bin/choco
            sudo chmod +x /usr/local/bin/choco
            choco help
      - steps: << parameters.publish_steps >>
      - store_artifacts:
          path: dist

  smoke-test:
    parameters:
      executor:
        type: executor
      install-steps:
        type: steps
    executor: << parameters.executor >>
    steps:
      - steps: << parameters.install-steps >>
      - run:
          name: Verify circleci binary
          command: circleci version

  # Matrixed over the executors rather than over the tags: only the architecture
  # needs a machine of its own, so each job checks both variants. Printing the
  # arch inside the container makes the log say which half of the manifest ran. A
  # tag missing this platform fails here anyway — the arm machine images carry no
  # binfmt, so there is nothing to silently emulate an amd64-only image with.
  smoke-test-docker:
    parameters:
      executor:
        type: executor
    executor: << parameters.executor >>
    steps:
      - run:
          name: Verify circleci/circleci-cli:v1
          command: docker run --rm circleci/circleci-cli:v1 sh -c 'uname -m; circleci version'
      - run:
          name: Verify circleci/circleci-cli:v1-alpine
          command: docker run --rm circleci/circleci-cli:v1-alpine sh -c 'uname -m; circleci version'

  docs:
    executor: linux
    steps:
      - setup
      - run:
          name: Generate reference and build the site
          command: task docs:build
      - run:
          name: Check internal links
          command: task docs:test
      - store_artifacts:
          path: docs/website/public
      - persist_to_workspace:
          root: .
          paths:
            - "docs/website/public"

  docs-publish:
    executor: linux
    steps:
      - setup
      - attach_workspace:
          at: .
      - run:
          name: Publish to gh-pages
          command: task ci:docs:publish

  ok-to-deploy:
    type: no-op

workflows:
  ci:
    jobs:
      # gh-pages holds only generated HTML — never run CI on it. Entry jobs (no
      # `requires`) must opt out explicitly; downstream jobs are gated by these.

      - check:
          filters:
            branches:
              ignore: gh-pages

      - test:
          matrix:
            parameters:
              executor:
                - linux
                - macos
                - windows
          filters:
            branches:
              ignore: gh-pages

      - docs:
          filters:
            branches:
              ignore: gh-pages

      - deploy:
          name: dry-run
          publish_steps:
            - run: task ci:build
          filters:
            branches:
              ignore:
                - main
                - gh-pages

      - ok-to-deploy:
          requires:
            - check
            - test
            - docs
          filters:
            branches:
              only: main

      - mark-release:
          requires:
            - ok-to-deploy

      - deploy:
          serial-group: << pipeline.project.slug >>/deploy
          requires:
            - ok-to-deploy
          context:
            - devex-release
            - macos-codesigning

      - docs-publish:
          serial-group: << pipeline.project.slug >>/docs-publish
          requires:
            - ok-to-deploy
          context:
            - devex-release

      - smoke-test:
          name: smoke-test-snap
          executor: linux
          install-steps:
            - run:
                name: Install snapd
                command: sudo apt update --yes && sudo apt install snapd --yes
            - run:
                name: Install circleci via Snap stable channel
                # /snap/bin has to be prepended, not just present: the machine
                # image ships its own circleci in /usr/local/bin, which would
                # otherwise shadow the snap and make this job verify the build
                # agent's CLI instead of the release.
                command: |
                  sudo snap install circleci
                  echo 'export PATH="/snap/bin:$PATH"' >> "$BASH_ENV"
          requires:
            - deploy
          filters:
            branches:
              only: main

      - smoke-test:
          name: smoke-test-brew
          executor: macos
          install-steps:
            - run:
                name: Install circleci via Homebrew preview tap
                command: |
                  brew update
                  rm -f /opt/homebrew/bin/circleci
                  brew install circleci-public/circleci/circleci@next
          requires:
            - deploy
          filters:
            branches:
              only: main

      - smoke-test-docker:
          matrix:
            parameters:
              executor:
                - linux
                - linux-arm
          requires:
            - deploy
          filters:
            branches:
              only: main

      - smoke-test:
          name: smoke-test-choco
          executor: windows
          install-steps:
            - run:
                name: Install circleci via Chocolatey
                command: choco install circleci-cli -y
          requires:
            - deploy
          filters:
            branches:
              only: main
